security_audit.summary: The static external command and network alerts are false positives from Markdown fences, inline code formatting, and example.com placeholder URLs. Semantic review found security guidance weaknesses in the CI examples, including disabled Kubernetes TLS verification, unsafe Docker password handling, and a vulnerability scan that can fail without blocking the pipeline.

remediation.issue: Kubernetes deployment example disables TLS certificate verification.
remediation.suggestion: Remove --insecure-skip-tls-verify and show trusted cluster CA configuration for GitLab CI deployments.

remediation.issue: Docker registry login passes the password with a command-line flag.
remediation.suggestion: Use a password-stdin pattern and keep registry credentials in masked, protected CI variables.

remediation.issue: The Trivy scan allows failures while checking high and critical vulnerabilities.
remediation.suggestion: Make high and critical scan results fail the pipeline, or document any exception policy clearly.

semantic_findings.title: Insecure Kubernetes TLS Verification Disabled
semantic_findings.description: The deployment template uses --insecure-skip-tls-verify=true, which teaches pipelines to ignore Kubernetes API certificate validation. This can expose deployments to man-in-the-middle attacks.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The insecure flag is directly present in the Kubernetes deployment example. Its security impact is clear and does not depend on user input.

semantic_findings.title: Registry Password Passed as CLI Argument
semantic_findings.description: The Docker login example passes CI_REGISTRY_PASSWORD through the -p option. Command-line arguments can expose secrets in logs or process metadata.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The pattern is visible in the Docker build example. GitLab masking can reduce exposure, but --password-stdin is the safer documented pattern.

semantic_findings.title: Critical Vulnerability Scan Allowed to Fail
semantic_findings.description: The Trivy job scans for HIGH and CRITICAL image vulnerabilities but allows the job to fail. Pipelines may continue after serious findings.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The scan severity filter and allow_failure setting are adjacent in the same job. This is a clear policy weakness in a security scanning example.

content.value_statement: GitLab CI/CD setup can become slow and inconsistent across build, test, and deploy stages. This skill provides reusable patterns for caching, runners, scans, Docker builds, Kubernetes deploys, Terraform, and child pipelines.
actual_capabilities: Provides staged GitLab CI YAML patterns for build, test, and deploy workflows.
Shows Docker image build and push jobs for GitLab Container Registry.
Includes Kubernetes deployment patterns for staging and production environments.
Covers Terraform validation, planning, and manual apply pipelines.
Describes caching, artifacts, security scanning, and dynamic child pipelines.
limitations: It provides examples and guidance; it does not execute or validate pipelines.
Examples need project-specific review before production use.
Some domains, image names, paths, and deployment names are placeholders.
Security-sensitive deployment patterns need hardening before publication.

use_cases.title: Create multi-stage pipelines
use_cases.description: Design build, test, and deploy jobs with artifacts, cache paths, and branch rules.

use_cases.title: Standardize Kubernetes deployments
use_cases.description: Create staging and production deployment jobs with manual production gates and environment tracking.

use_cases.title: Add infrastructure workflows
use_cases.description: Draft Terraform validation, plan, and apply stages for infrastructure changes in GitLab.

prompt_templates.title: Start a basic pipeline
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a small application.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a simple GitLab CI pipeline for my project with build, test, and deploy stages. Include cache and artifact recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Add Docker publishing
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add Docker image build and push jobs to GitLab CI. Use GitLab registry variables and explain required protected variables.

prompt_templates.title: Design environment deploys
prompt_templates.prompt: Design GitLab CI jobs for staging and production Kubernetes deployments. Include manual production approval and safe secret handling.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a complex pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my GitLab CI pipeline for caching, artifacts, runner usage, child pipelines, security scans, and Terraform workflow risks.

output_examples.input: I need a GitLab CI pipeline for a Node service.
output: A staged pipeline plan for build, lint, test, and deploy jobs.
Cache and artifact recommendations for dependencies and build outputs.
Branch and environment rules for safer deployment behavior.

output_examples.input: I want Docker images built and pushed from GitLab.
output: A container publishing workflow using GitLab registry variables.
Credential handling notes for protected and masked CI variables.
Tagging guidance for commit-specific and release images.

output_examples.input: I need Terraform in GitLab CI.
output: A validation, plan, and apply workflow outline.
Artifact handling guidance for plan files.
Manual approval guidance for infrastructure changes.

best_practices: Use pinned container image versions and review upgrades on a schedule.
Keep production deployments behind manual approvals and protected branches.
Store secrets in masked, protected GitLab CI variables or a dedicated secrets manager.
anti_patterns: Do not copy placeholder domains, namespaces, or deployment names without review.
Do not disable TLS verification for Kubernetes API access.
Do not allow critical security scans to fail silently in production pipelines.

faq.question: Does this skill execute GitLab pipelines?
faq.answer: No. It provides pipeline patterns and review guidance for users to adapt.

faq.question: Can it help with GitLab Runner configuration?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide runner-related choices, but users must configure their own runner infrastructure.

faq.question: Does it cover Kubernetes deployments?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes staging and production deployment patterns that should be hardened before use.

faq.question: Does it include Terraform workflow guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers validation, planning, artifacts, manual apply gates, and main-branch restrictions.

faq.question: Is this suitable for production pipelines?
faq.answer: It can be a starting point, but security settings and project values need review before production use.
